explainers.title: The order that starts it all
explainers.takeaway: An order promises the bags. It doesn't move them yet.
explainers.dek: Corner Cup Cafe wants 30 bags. Raju puts his first quote into ERPNext, and learns what an order does and doesn't do.
explainers.so_far: The Coffee Company is trying ERPNext. The Frappe Guy has set up a real ERPNext site for it, with its bags, its cafes and its stock.

panels.caption: Corner Cup Cafe calls Raju.
panels.left_bubble: Twenty bags of the Ethiopian and ten of House Blend? I'll send you a price today.
Before, this went into a sheet. Where does it go now?
panels.right_bubble: First, ERPNext needs three things: what you sell, who buys it, and where it's kept.

panels.caption: Salman, who designs the coffee bags, is listening.
panels.left_bubble: Do those things have names in ERPNext?

panels.right_bubble: Each bag you sell is an Item. Each cafe is a Customer. Each store room is a Warehouse.

panels.caption: The Ethiopian roast as an Item: its name, its group and its tax code. Maintain Stock is ticked, so ERPNext counts every bag.
panels.screen_alt: ERPNext Item form for Ethiopian Roast, 250 g bag: item group Products, HSN tax code 090121, Maintain Stock ticked.

panels.left_bubble: So now I write the order?
panels.right_bubble: Not yet. First a Quotation: the price you offer before the cafe says yes.

panels.caption: Raju fills in the quote. Until he submits it, it stays a Draft.
panels.screen_alt: A new Quotation for Corner Cup Cafe dated 06-11-2026, marked Draft, with a Submit button and the note: Submit this document to confirm.

panels.left_bubble: What's the difference between saving and submitting?
panels.right_bubble: A draft is a scratch copy you can change. Submit it, and it becomes final and locked.

panels.left_bubble: Locked? What if I got a price wrong?
panels.right_bubble: Cancel it, then Amend. ERPNext makes a fresh copy to fix. The old one stays on record.

panels.caption: Submitted. The quote is Open: 20 Ethiopian and 10 House Blend for Corner Cup, valid for a week, ₹11,800 in all.
panels.screen_alt: Submitted Quotation for Corner Cup Cafe, status Open, dated 06-11-2026, valid till 13-11-2026, items ETH-250 quantity 20 and HOUSE-250 quantity 10, total ₹11,800.

panels.left_bubble: Corner Cup said yes this morning. Do I type it all again as an order?
panels.right_bubble: No. On the quote, Create, then Sales Order. It becomes the cafe's confirmed order.

panels.caption: The Sales Order: same cafe, same bags, and a delivery date. Its status says what is left to do: deliver and bill.
panels.screen_alt: Sales Order for Corner Cup Cafe, status To Deliver and Bill, dated 07-11-2026, delivery date 09-11-2026, items ETH-250 quantity 20 and HOUSE-250 quantity 10, total ₹11,800.

panels.caption: Ishita, who runs The Coffee Company, has been listening.
panels.left_bubble: So the 20 bags have left the shelf?

panels.right_bubble: Not yet. A Sales Order promises the bags. It doesn't move them.

panels.caption: The roast's stock right now: 24 bags on the shelf, 20 promised to Corner Cup, and 4 free to promise to anyone else.
panels.screen_alt: Stock Projected Qty report for ETH-250: Actual Qty 24, Reserved Qty 20, Projected Qty 4.

panels.left_bubble: So before I promise a cafe, I check what's free. Four, not twenty-four.
panels.right_bubble: And everyone sees the same number.

panels.left_bubble: And if I promise more bags than we have?
panels.right_bubble: It lets you take the order. By default, it won't let anyone send out bags that aren't on the shelf.

panels.caption: Try to send out 30 bags of the Ethiopian when only 24 are on the shelf, and ERPNext refuses: 6 short.
panels.screen_alt: ERPNext message titled Insufficient Stock: 6.0 units of Item ETH-250, Ethiopian Roast, 250 g bag, needed in Warehouse Packed Bags - TCC to complete this transaction.

panels.caption: One cafe order, five documents. Each is made from the one before.
panels.diagram_labels:
#+ Quotation
- The offer
#+ Sales Order
- The promise
# Delivery Note
- Bags leave
# Sales Invoice
- Money owed
# Payment Entry
- Money in

panels.left_bubble: So when do the bags actually leave?
panels.right_bubble: Tomorrow morning, at the roastery. Bring Sara. She'll want to see the money.

explainers.title: From roastery to paid
explainers.takeaway: Each step is its own document, made from the last, so nothing is typed twice.
explainers.dek: The bags leave, the bill goes out, the money comes in. Sara follows Corner Cup's order to the bank, one document at a time.
explainers.so_far: Raju's quote for Corner Cup Cafe became a Sales Order. ERPNext has promised the cafe 20 bags of the Ethiopian roast and 10 of House Blend. None has left yet.

panels.caption: Next morning. Sara, who keeps the numbers, joins them.
panels.left_bubble: The order's sold. Show me how the money gets from the cafe to us.

panels.right_bubble: Follow the bags first. Whoever packs the order makes a Delivery Note from the Sales Order.

panels.left_bubble: A Delivery Note being?
panels.right_bubble: The record of what left, for whom, from which warehouse. It's what moves the stock.

panels.caption: The Delivery Note for Corner Cup: 20 Ethiopian and 10 House Blend, taken from the Sales Order. Nothing retyped.
panels.screen_alt: Delivery Note for Corner Cup Cafe, status To Bill, dated 08-11-2026, items ETH-250 quantity 20 and HOUSE-250 quantity 10.

panels.caption: Submit it, and the shelf count drops: 24 bags of the roast become 4, and nothing is promised any more.
panels.screen_alt: Stock Projected Qty report for ETH-250 after the delivery: Actual Qty 4, Reserved Qty 0, Projected Qty 4.

panels.left_bubble: Stock, fine. The bill?
panels.right_bubble: A Sales Invoice, made from the Delivery Note. It says what Corner Cup owes, and by when.

panels.caption: The Sales Invoice: ₹11,800, due in two weeks, status Unpaid. The whole amount is still outstanding.
panels.screen_alt: Sales Invoice for Corner Cup Cafe, status Unpaid, posting date 08-11-2026, payment due date 22-11-2026, grand total ₹11,800, outstanding amount ₹11,800.

panels.left_bubble: No GST on it?
panels.right_bubble: This demo company isn't registered for GST yet. GST gets its own part, in ERPNext III.

panels.caption: Salman, who designs the bags, has a question.
panels.left_bubble: Why two documents? Couldn't the invoice move the stock too?

panels.right_bubble: It can. For a sale at the counter, tick Update Stock and one invoice does both.
But cafes get the bags first and pay later. Two documents record each step when it really happens.

panels.caption: That afternoon, Corner Cup pays by bank transfer.
panels.left_bubble: The money's in the bank. Does the invoice know?

panels.right_bubble: Once you record it. A Payment Entry: money received, matched to that invoice.

panels.caption: The Payment Entry: Receive, by wire transfer, ₹11,800 from Corner Cup, against that one invoice.
panels.screen_alt: Payment Entry, submitted, payment type Receive, posting date 08-11-2026, mode of payment Wire Transfer, paid amount ₹11,800, referencing Sales Invoice SINV-26-00001.

panels.caption: And the invoice changes by itself: Paid, nothing outstanding.
panels.screen_alt: The same Sales Invoice, now marked Paid, with outstanding amount ₹0.00.

panels.left_bubble: And when someone types 15 instead of 20 on the delivery? I've seen it happen.

panels.right_bubble: Undo newest first: the payment, the invoice, then the delivery. Then amend the delivery. ERPNext lists what's linked.

panels.caption: Every document links to the rest. The order's Connections show its delivery and its invoice. Delivered and billed, it says Completed.
panels.screen_alt: Sales Order for Corner Cup Cafe, status Completed, Connections tab showing one Sales Invoice and one Delivery Note.

panels.caption: What each document changes.
panels.diagram_labels:
# Quotation
- Nothing moves
# Sales Order
- Bags promised
# Delivery Note
- Stock goes down
# Sales Invoice
- Money owed
# Payment Entry
- Money in

panels.caption: Raju bursts in.
panels.left_bubble: Blue Door Cafe wants 60 bags. Can I give them a better price?

explainers.title: Cafe prices and online prices
explainers.takeaway: Price lists hold your prices. Pricing rules apply discounts by themselves when every condition matches.
explainers.dek: Cafes pay one price, online buyers another, and 60 bags get 5% off. Raju learns where prices live and how a discount applies itself.
explainers.so_far: Corner Cup Cafe's order went from quote to paid, one document at a time. Now Blue Door Cafe wants 60 bags of House Blend.

panels.left_bubble: Blue Door wants 60 bags of House Blend. For that many, I want to give 5% off.
Where does our price even come from?
panels.right_bubble: From a Price List. You set up two: Cafe Prices and Online Prices.
Each list holds a price per item. House Blend is ₹340 a bag for cafes and ₹420 online.

panels.caption: Salman, who designs the bags, is curious.
panels.left_bubble: How does a quote know Blue Door is a cafe?

panels.right_bubble: Customers sit in groups. Blue Door is in the Cafes group, and Cafes use Cafe Prices.

panels.caption: The Cafes customer group. Its default price list is Cafe Prices, so every cafe's quote starts there.
panels.screen_alt: Customer Group Cafes, parent All Customer Groups, default price list Cafe Prices.

panels.left_bubble: And the 5%? Do I type it on every big order?
panels.right_bubble: No. Write it once as a Pricing Rule. ERPNext applies it when the conditions match.

panels.caption: The rule: for the Cafes group, on Cafe Prices, at 50 bags or more, take 5% off anything in the Products group.
panels.screen_alt: Pricing Rule titled Cafes: 5% off 50 bags or more. Applied on item group Products, for selling, for customer group Cafes, minimum quantity 50, discount percentage 5, for price list Cafe Prices.

panels.caption: Raju quotes Blue Door.
panels.left_bubble: Sixty bags of House Blend. Let's see what happens.

panels.caption: The line on Raju's quote: list price ₹340, rate ₹323. The rule took 5% off by itself. For 60 bags: ₹19,380.
panels.screen_alt: Quotation item row for HOUSE-250, House Blend, 250 g bag: quantity 60, price list rate ₹340, rate ₹323, amount ₹19,380.

panels.left_bubble: It did the maths for me.
panels.right_bubble: Because every condition matched: a cafe, cafe prices, and 50 bags or more.

panels.caption: Sara has been reading the quote.
panels.left_bubble: Same quote for 40 bags?

panels.right_bubble: Full price, ₹340 a bag. 40 is under 50, so the rule stays off.

panels.left_bubble: And someone ordering online?
panels.right_bubble: Online Prices, ₹420 a bag, and no cafe discount, even for 60.

panels.left_bubble: What if two rules match one order?
panels.right_bubble: Give them priorities, so ERPNext knows which one wins. Then test it on a quote first.

panels.caption: How Blue Door's price is chosen.
panels.diagram_labels:
# Blue Door Cafe
- The customer
# Cafes group
- Picks Cafe Prices
# Cafe Prices
- House Blend ₹340
#+ Pricing Rule
- 5% off at 50+
# Quote
- ₹323 a bag

panels.caption: Ishita walks in from the roastery.
panels.left_bubble: Selling looks fine. Now show them how we bought the green beans this week.

explainers.title: Buying green beans
explainers.takeaway: Buying runs like selling: each document made from the last, from the request to the payment.
explainers.dek: The Ethiopian green beans run low. Ishita follows one purchase from the first request to paying the exporter.
explainers.so_far: Selling now runs through ERPNext, from quote to payment. This part goes back to the start of that week, when the Ethiopian green beans ran low.

panels.caption: Earlier that week. Ishita, who runs The Coffee Company, is short of beans.
panels.left_bubble: We need 60 kilos of Ethiopian green beans. Usually I just phone the exporter.

panels.right_bubble: Start with a Material Request: a note that says we need this. It buys nothing yet.

panels.caption: The Material Request, which ERPNext titles a purchase request: 60 kg of Ethiopian green beans for the Green Beans store room, needed by the 5th.
panels.screen_alt: Material Request, status Pending, purpose Purchase, transaction date 02-11-2026, required by 05-11-2026, warehouse Green Beans - TCC, item GB-ETH quantity 60.

panels.caption: Salman, who designs the bags, looks puzzled.
panels.left_bubble: Why write a note? Just buy the beans.

panels.right_bubble: Today Ishita does both. As you grow, they're different people, and the note connects them.

panels.left_bubble: I buy from Highland, in Ethiopia.
panels.right_bubble: Then Highland is a Supplier. Turn the request into a Purchase Order: your order to them.

panels.caption: The Purchase Order to Highland: 60 kg at ₹900 a kilo, ₹54,000. Still to receive, still to bill.
panels.screen_alt: Purchase Order to Highland Green Coffee Exports, status To Receive and Bill, dated 02-11-2026, required by 05-11-2026, item GB-ETH quantity 60, total ₹54,000.

panels.caption: Three days later, the sacks arrive.
panels.left_bubble: They're here. Do I just tick the order off?

panels.right_bubble: Count them in with a Purchase Receipt. It's the mirror of a Delivery Note: stock comes in.

panels.caption: The Purchase Receipt: 60 kg from Highland, into the Green Beans store room. Now the beans are in stock.
panels.screen_alt: Purchase Receipt from Highland Green Coffee Exports, status To Bill, dated 05-11-2026, accepted warehouse Green Beans - TCC, item GB-ETH accepted quantity 60.

panels.caption: Sara has the supplier's bill.
panels.left_bubble: Received isn't paid. Highland has sent its bill.

panels.right_bubble: Their bill becomes a Purchase Invoice: what you owe them. A Payment Entry pays it, like Corner Cup's.

panels.caption: The Purchase Invoice: ₹54,000 owed to Highland, made from the receipt so the numbers match.
panels.screen_alt: Purchase Invoice from Highland Green Coffee Exports, status Unpaid, posting date 05-11-2026, grand total ₹54,000, outstanding amount ₹54,000.

panels.left_bubble: It's the selling chain, the other way round.
panels.right_bubble: Same idea. Each document is made from the one before.

panels.caption: Received and billed, so the order says Completed. Its Connections show the receipt and the invoice. Highland was paid the next day.
panels.screen_alt: Purchase Order to Highland Green Coffee Exports, status Completed, Connections tab showing one Purchase Receipt and one Purchase Invoice.

panels.left_bubble: Do we need all five steps every time?
panels.right_bubble: No. On a new site you can skip the request, order and receipt. Buying Settings can require the last two.

panels.caption: Buying, step by step. The receipt is where stock comes in.
panels.diagram_labels:
# Material Request
- We need it
# Purchase Order
- We ordered it
#+ Purchase Receipt
- Stock comes in
# Purchase Invoice
- We owe it
# Payment Entry
- Money out

panels.left_bubble: ₹900 a kilo. But we also paid for freight and a clearing agent. Where did that go?

explainers.title: What an imported bean really costs
explainers.takeaway: Add freight and clearing to the beans with a Landed Cost Voucher, so every bag carries its real cost.
explainers.dek: The beans cost ₹900 a kilo, plus freight, plus a clearing agent. Sara makes ERPNext count the real cost.
explainers.so_far: The Coffee Company bought 60 kg of Ethiopian green beans at ₹900 a kilo. Freight and a clearing agent cost extra. Sara wants to know where that went.

panels.caption: Sara, who keeps the numbers, has the other bills.
panels.left_bubble: Freight was ₹4,800. The clearing agent, ₹4,200. That's ₹9,000 on top of the beans.

panels.right_bubble: Then the beans cost more than ₹900 a kilo. First, how ERPNext values stock.
Every kilo in stock has a value: what it cost you. ERPNext calls it the valuation rate.

panels.caption: The report's average rate is the valuation rate: ₹900 a kilo, so 60 kg are worth ₹54,000. The freight isn't in it.
panels.screen_alt: Stock Ledger for GB-ETH: in quantity 60, balance quantity 60, average rate ₹900, balance value ₹54,000.

panels.caption: Salman, who designs the bags, shrugs.
panels.left_bubble: Does it matter? The money's spent either way.

panels.right_bubble: Leave it out and every roasted bag looks cheaper than it is, and its profit looks bigger than it is.

panels.left_bubble: So how do I add it?
panels.right_bubble: With a Landed Cost Voucher. You attach the charges to the Purchase Receipt they belong to.

panels.caption: Sara's Landed Cost Voucher: sea freight ₹4,800 and the clearing agent ₹4,200, against Highland's receipt, split by quantity.
panels.screen_alt: Landed Cost Voucher, submitted, dated 07-11-2026, for Purchase Receipt PR-26-00001, with charges Sea freight for the beans ₹4,800 and Port and clearing agent ₹4,200, distributed based on Qty.

panels.left_bubble: Split how, if one delivery has two kinds of beans?
panels.right_bubble: You choose: by quantity, by amount, or by hand.

panels.caption: Submitted. The same 60 kg are now worth ₹63,000: ₹1,050 a kilo. ERPNext updated the receipt's value itself.
panels.screen_alt: Stock Ledger for GB-ETH after the Landed Cost Voucher: in quantity 60, balance quantity 60, average rate ₹1,050, balance value ₹63,000.

panels.caption: ₹54,000 plus ₹9,000 is ₹63,000. Over 60 kg, that's ₹1,050 a kilo.
panels.diagram_labels:
# Beans
- 60 kg, ₹54,000
# + Freight
- ₹4,800
# + Clearing agent
- ₹4,200
#+ = Real cost
- ₹1,050 a kilo

panels.left_bubble: Now that number I believe.
panels.right_bubble: Record the roasting in ERPNext and every bag made from these beans carries it. That's ERPNext II.

panels.left_bubble: Any catch?
panels.right_bubble: Book freight as a plain expense and the stock never knows. Attach it to the receipt.

panels.caption: ERPNext I, in one box: what ERPNext does for buying and selling, how, and what comes later.
panels.diagram_labels:
# Quote to payment
- Built in
# Cafe and online prices
- Built in
# Big-order discounts
- Built in
# Request to payment
- Built in
# Freight in bean cost
- Built in

panels.caption: Ishita has followed every step.
panels.left_bubble: Buying and selling: yes. And what happens to the beans once they're here?
